paragraphs: Children in care in Dumfries and Galloway are looked after by Dumfries and Galloway Council's Fostering and Adoption team, shown above with the independent services that take enquiries from the region. The council needs homes for children from babies to teenagers, and particularly for brothers and sisters who need to stay together, mothers and babies, children with additional needs, and asylum-seeking children, whose numbers it says are growing.

Its carers work in four main ways: short break care at weekends and in the holidays; interim care, a home for up to 24 months when a child first comes into care; permanent care into adulthood; and its Intensive Support Service, round-the-clock care for young people with the highest needs, which asks for a full-time carer with experience of trauma and no birth children under 18 at home.

You need to be over 21, with no upper age limit, reasonably fit and healthy, and have a spare room big enough for a single bed and storage. Being single, renting, working or having children of your own does not stop you. Carers meet a worker from the team at least monthly, join support groups and a buddy scheme, and take an annual training programme, with Fostering Network membership paid by the council. The council pays a weekly fee and an allowance for each child, with extra weeks at Christmas, birthdays and in the summer holidays and mileage at 45p a mile; its support page does not say which year its figures cover, so ask the team for current rates.

From April 2026 the Scottish Recommended Allowance, the national minimum for a child's costs, is £177.68 a week for ages 0 to 4, £206.71 for 5 to 15 and £283.35 for 16 and 17; any carer fee is paid on top.

In 2026 the council adopted a Fostering Friendly policy giving its own staff up to ten days' paid leave a year for fostering commitments, and The Fostering Network recognised it as a Fostering Friendly employer. For the rest of the country, see our Scotland page.
